codeReview.summary: Clean, well-structured implementation of lib/factory-usage.js with four exported functions (computeBillingPeriod, sumDailyTokens, extractModelBreakdown, fetchFactoryUsage). Follows the parallel module pattern established by codex-usage.js and claude-usage.js. All feature requirements met: correct API URL construction with date params, JWT-preferred auth with apiKey fallback, AbortController timeout, structured return format, billing period edge case handling, and input validation. 49 tests added covering all specified scenarios. Barrel re-exports properly added to shuvquota.js.

issues.description: computeBillingPeriod accepts non-integer billingDay values (e.g., 1.5). The Date constructor truncates to integer so it works, but the feature description says 'reject non-numeric' — fractional days arguably should be rejected for strictness. Low impact since no real-world caller would pass a fractional day.

Date arithmetic in computeBillingPeriod uses local timezone (new Date(year, month, day)) rather than UTC. The mission AGENTS.md notes 'Date params: startDate and endDate in YYYY-MM-DD (UTC)'. In practice this is fine since billing periods are day-level granularity and the formatted output is date-only, but a timezone-sensitive deployment near midnight could theoretically shift the reference date. Very low risk for a CLI tool.

planLimit is read from account object (account?.planLimit ?? 0) but the Factory API response format documented in AGENTS.md doesn't include a planLimit field. This means the caller must inject planLimit from external knowledge (e.g., FACTORY_PLAN_TIERS in constants.js). This is a design choice that works but differs from how codex-usage.js returns raw API data without computing percent. Consistent with the feature spec which requires returning { percent }.

summary: Feature factory-usage passes review. The implementation is clean, follows all project conventions (tabs, double quotes, semicolons, JSDoc, section dividers, ESM imports with node: prefix, error-return pattern, AbortController timeout). All four functions work correctly with comprehensive test coverage (49 tests). Three non-blocking observations noted: fractional billingDay acceptance, local timezone date math, and planLimit sourcing from account object rather than API response. No blocking issues found.
